Rally length, serve direction (wide/body/T), return depth, how the point ended, net approaches and the stroke of every shot are parsed from each point's shot string; the point is played from the second-serve string when the first is a fault
infosys: 37908 distinct matches (37908 singles: codes MS and QS); doubles left out

Rally length is the shot that ended the point (serve, return, 3rd ... 8th, then '9+ odd' and '10+ even'); serve speed, serve direction, net flags and stroke per point; per-set key statistics (winners, unforced errors, net points won, serve speeds) are counted as match totals
court_vision: 4570 files; 4566 placed through an Infosys record of the same year, tournament and match code; 0 unreadable
Counted as ball tracking only here; its per-stroke fields (speeds, spin, positions) use obfuscated keys that a later stage would decode against the readable Slam copy
slam_pbp: Ending counts points flagged ace, double fault, winner, unforced or forced error; net play counts points with a net-point flag; which columns are filled varies by Slam and year
slamtracker: Ending counts points flagged winner, unforced error, ace or double fault (forced errors are not flagged in these feeds, so about two thirds of points carry an ending)
slam_tracking: Dated three days after the Slam's first day, as the data map does (the copy has no match dates); every stroke's trajectory only for 2022-2024
wta_advanced: 29361 singles matches listed 2019-2026; 24309 with an advanced-statistics file on disk (raw files read directly; the staged table holds a sample only; the download chain that writes other files beside them was left running)
